answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It survives because finality only counts for established attestators, so a fresh cluster cannot push transactions until it proves honesty across many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a lagoon as the anchor of the cost. A fable stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a haven holds...
